questions.question:
Two statements are given followed by three conclusions numbered I, II and III. Assuming the statements to be true, even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements.

**Statements:**

All pigeons are crows.

No crow is a bird.

**Conclusions:**

I. Some crows are pigeons.

II. Some pigeons are birds.

III. No pigeon is a bird.

options.text: Only conclusions I and II follow.
Either conclusion II or III follows.
Only conclusions I and III follow
Only conclusions II and III follow.

questions.solution:
Statements:

All pigeons are crows.

No crow is a bird.

The least possible diagram for the given statements is as follows

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/8be293f3f8c76b17ca6d69e7a2d0fa1de0a5c6510cd468f1906e1c4cc4731ead.png] 

Conclusions:

I. Some crows are pigeons → True (because all pigeons are crows and so some crows are also pigeons)

II. Some pigeons are birds → False (because all pigeons are crows and no crow is a bird so no pigeon is also a bird)

III. No pigeon is a bird → True (because all pigeons are crows and no crow is a bird so no pigeon is also a bird)

Hence, “**Only conclusions I and III follow**”.

questions.question: Among five iron balls P, Q, R, S and T, the weight of Q is 5 kg, which is double the weight of P, The weight of S is half the weight of T. The weight of R is equal to the weight of P and Q taken together. The weight of T is four times the weight of R. What is the weight of S?
questions.solution:
Total five iron balls: - P, Q, R, S and T

**1) The weight of Q is 5 kg, which is double the weight of P.**

=> Q = 5 kg **--------- eq. (1)**

And,

=> Q = 2P kg

So, P = Q / 2 = 5 / 2 = 2.5 kg **--------- eq. (2)**

**2) The weight of S is half the weight of T.**

=> S = T / 2 kg **--------- eq. (3)**

**3) The weight of R is equal to the weight of P and Q taken together.**

=> R = P + Q = 2.5 + 5 = 7.5 kg **--------- eq. (4)** (Value of P and Q taken from eq. (2) and (1))

**4) The weight of T is four times the weight of R.**

=> T = 4R = 4 × 7.5 = 30 kg **--------- eq. (5)**

From eq. (3),

=> S = T / 2

=> S = 30 / 2 (Value of T is taken from eq. (5))

**=> S = 15 kg**

Hence, weight of the S is **“15 kg”.**

questions.question:
Which two signs should be interchanging to make the given equation correct?

32 + 14 × 3 – 91 ÷ 7 = 3
questions.solution:
According to the BODMAS rule:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/2042326d26ec7b593e52bbbdd22d890b59b1e59f92be81a7235509e9af1c4625.png] 

**Option 1 :** + and –

**Given:**

**32 + 14 × 3 – 91 ÷ 7 = 3**

**After interchange the signs;**

**32 - 14 × 3 + 91 ÷ 7 = 3**

**By BODMAS rule**

**32 - 14 × 3 + 13 = 3**

**32 - 42 + 13 = 3**

**45 - 42 = 3**

**3 = 3**** (LHS = RHS)**

**Option 2 : **+ and × 

Given:

32 + 14 × 3 – 91 ÷ 7 = 3

After interchange the signs;

32 × 14 + 3 – 91 ÷ 7 = 3

By BODMAS rule

32 × 14 + 3 – 13 = 3

448 + 3 – 13 = 3

451 – 13 = 3

438 = 3** (LHS ≠ RHS)**

**Option 3 :** ÷ and –

Given:

32 + 14 × 3 – 91 ÷ 7 = 3

After interchange the signs;

32 + 14 × 3 ÷ 91 - 7 = 3

By BODMAS rule

32 + 14 × 0.33 - 7 = 3

32 + 4.62 - 7 = 3

36.62 - 7 = 3

29.62 = 3** (LHS ≠ RHS)**

**Option 4 :** ÷ and × 

Given:

32 + 14 × 3 – 91 ÷ 7 = 3

After interchange the signs;

32 + 14 ÷ 3 – 91 × 7 = 3

By BODMAS rule

32 + 4.67 – 91 × 7 = 3

32 + 4.67 – 637 = 3

36.67 – 637 = 3

- 600.33 = 3** (LHS ≠ RHS)**

Hence, the answer is **“****+ and –”.**

questions.question:
Study the given pattern carefully and select the number that can replace the question mark (?) in it.

 
 

 445
 285
 80
 
 

 550
 332
 109
 
 

 655
 441
 ?
questions.solution:
Here the pattern followed in **each row** is:

**(1st number - 2nd number) ÷ 2 = 3rd number**

Row 1: 445 285 80

(1st number - 2nd number) ÷ 2 = 3rd number

= (445 - 285) ÷ 2

= 160 ÷ 2

= 80 = 3rd number

Row 2: 550 332 109

(1st number - 2nd number) ÷ 2 = 3rd number

= (550 - 332) ÷ 2

= 218 ÷ 2

= 109 = 3rd number

Similarly,

**Row 3: **655 441 ?

**(1st number - 2nd ****number**)** ÷ 2 = 3rd number**

**= (655 - 441) ÷ 2**

**= 214 ÷ 2**

**= 107 = 3rd number**

**Hence, “107” is correct answer.**

questions.question:

72 + 63 ÷ 9 × 5 – 36 = 67
questions.solution:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/2042326d26ec7b593e52bbbdd22d890b59b1e59f92be81a7235509e9af1c4625.png] 

**Option 1 :** 63 and 36

Given:

72 + 63 ÷ 9 × 5 – 36 = 67

After interchange the signs;

72 + 36 ÷ 9 × 5 – 63 = 67

**By BODMAS rule**

72 + 4 × 5 – 63 = 67

72 + 20 – 63 = 67

92 – 63 = 67

29 = 67 **(LHS ≠ RHS)**

**Option 2 : **63 and 72

**Given:**

**72 + 63 ÷ 9 × 5 – 36 = 67**

**After interchange the signs;**

**63 + 72 ÷ 9 × 5 – 36 = 67**

**By BODMAS rule**

**63 + 72 ÷ 9 × 5 – 36 = 67**

**63 + 8 × 5 – 36 = 67**

**63 + 40 – 36 = 67**

**103 – 36 = 67**

**67 = 67 (LHS = RHS)**

**Option 3 :** 5 and 36

Given:

72 + 63 ÷ 9 × 5 – 36 = 67

After interchange the signs;

72 + 63 ÷ 9 × 36 – 5 = 67

By BODMAS rule

72 + 7 × 36 – 5 = 67

72 + 252 – 5 = 67

322 – 5 = 67

317 = 67** (LHS ≠ RHS)**

**Option 4 :** 72 and 36

Given:

72 + 63 ÷ 9 × 5 – 36 = 67

After interchange the signs;

36 + 63 ÷ 9 × 5 – 72 = 67

By BODMAS rule

36 + 63 ÷ 9 × 5 – 72 = 67

36 + 7 × 5 – 72 = 67

36 + 35 – 72 = 67

71 – 72 = 67

- 1 = 67** (LHS ≠ RHS)**

Hence, the answer is **“****63 and 72”.**

questions.question:
Select the option that is related to the third number in the same way as the second number is related to the first number.

20 : 421 :: 18 : ?
questions.solution:
The pattern followed here is,

**Let (1st number : 2ⁿd number)**

**(1st number)² + (1st number + 1) = 2ⁿd number**

Now follow the steps:

20 : 421

=> 20² + (20 + 1) = 400 + 21 = 421 = 2ⁿd number

Similarly,

**18 : ?**

**=> 18² + (18 + 1) = 324 + 19 = 343 = 2ⁿd number**

Hence, **"343"** is correct answer.

questions.question:
Two statements are given followed by two conclusions numbered I and II. Assuming the statements to be true, even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements.

**Statements:**

All machines are refrigerators.

All refrigerators are geysers.

**Conclusions:**

I. Some machines are not geysers.

II. Some geysers are machines.

options.text: Neither conclusion I nor II follows.
Both conclusions I and II follow.

questions.solution:
Statements:

All machines are refrigerators.

All refrigerators are geysers.

The least possible diagram for the given statements is as follows

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/b8b6a9ac1c409f0f8be3635d8929299711503d8490053dfd9530118819ecbb6d.png] 

Conclusions:

I. Some machines are not geysers → False (It is not possible because all machines are refrigerators and all refrigerators are geysers so some machines are definitely geyser)

II. Some geysers are machines → True (because all machines are refrigerators and all refrigerators are geysers so some geysers are definitely machines)

__
 
• Some + Some not - It is not a complementary pair.

Hence, “**Only conclusion II follows**”.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

Conditions of Either-or case:

1. Individually both the conclusions should be false.

2. One conclusion should be positive and one conclusion should be negative (Complementary pair)

The two complementary pairs are:

1) All + Some not

2) No + Some

 
• Some + Some not - It is not a complementary pair.
